mockTests.title: UGC NET Mock Test 4 - Nutrition Science & Dietetics
mockTests.description: Comprehensive simulation covering human nutrition, biochemistry, diet therapy, and food science standards.

questions.question: Which of the following amino acids is an essential precursor for the synthesis of Niacin (Vitamin B3)?
questions.explanation: Tryptophan is an essential amino acid that serves as a precursor for the endogenous synthesis of niacin (approx 60 mg tryptophan yields 1 mg niacin).

questions.question: Which enzyme is responsible for the rate-limiting step in endogenous cholesterol synthesis?
questions.explanation: HMG-CoA Reductase converts HMG-CoA to mevalonate, which is the primary rate-limiting step in cholesterol biosynthesis.

questions.question: In chronic kidney disease (CKD Stage 3-4), what is the typically recommended dietary protein intake for non-dialysis patients?
questions.explanation: KDOQI Clinical Practice Guidelines recommend protein restriction of 0.55-0.60 g/kg/day or 0.6-0.8 g/kg/day to slow progression of renal failure in non-dialysis CKD.

questions.question: The Maillard reaction in food processing involves a chemical reaction between:
questions.explanation: The Maillard reaction is a non-enzymatic browning reaction between amino acids and reducing sugars under heat.

questions.question: Which vitamin deficiency is specifically associated with Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome?
questions.explanation: Thiamine (Vitamin B1) deficiency, frequently seen in chronic alcoholism or severe malnutrition, causes Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome.

questions.question: What is the primary indicator of long-term glycemic control over a 2-3 month period?
questions.explanation: HbA1c reflects average blood glucose levels over the preceding 8-12 weeks based on red blood cell turnover.

questions.question: Which mineral is a key structural constituent of the antioxidant enzyme Glutathione Peroxidase?
questions.explanation: Selenium is incorporated as selenocysteine into the active site of glutathione peroxidase.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the respiratory quotient (RQ) for pure carbohydrate oxidation?
questions.explanation: The RQ for carbohydrate oxidation is 1.00 (VCO2 / VO2 = 6 / 6 = 1.0), whereas fat oxidation has an RQ of approximately 0.70.

questions.question: What is the critical temperature range known as the 'Food Temperature Danger Zone' in food safety?
questions.explanation: The danger zone between 5°C and 60°C (41°F - 140°F) facilitates rapid bacterial multiplication.

questions.question: Which bioactive compound in green tea is primarily responsible for its potent antioxidant capacity?
questions.explanation: EGCG is the most abundant and potent catechin polyphenol found in green tea.

mockTests.title: Quick Revision Quiz: Micronutrients & Food Chemistry
mockTests.description: Quick fire rounds to test retention on essential minerals, fat-soluble vitamins, and nutritional biochemistry.

questions.question: Which vitamin enhances the intestinal absorption of non-heme iron?
questions.explanation: Ascorbic acid reduces ferric iron (Fe3+) to ferrous iron (Fe2+), significantly improving bioavailability.

questions.question: Rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults are classically caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Vitamin D deficiency causes impaired mineralization of bone matrix, leading to rickets or osteomalacia.

questions.question: The conversion of beta-carotene into Vitamin A predominantly takes place in the:
questions.explanation: Intestinal enterocytes express beta-carotene 15,15'-dioxygenase, converting beta-carotene into retinal.

questions.question: Which of the following fatty acids is an essential omega-3 fatty acid?
questions.explanation: ALA (18:3 n-3) is the parent essential omega-3 fatty acid required in human nutrition.

questions.question: Which enzyme converts starch into maltose during salivary and pancreatic digestion?
questions.explanation: Alpha-amylase hydrolyzes internal alpha-1,4-glycosidic bonds in starch into maltose and dextrins.
